audit.whatIsWrong: Rows 0 through 4 all disagree with the published mirror.
audit.why: The mirror audit (irelia__warwick) set Warwick, Skill, Irelia, Warwick, Irelia, Warwick, Warwick as matched pairs on both layers. This side read Skill, Warwick, Warwick, Skill, Skill, Warwick, Warwick.
audit.corrected: Rows 0-4 flipped on both layers as one atomic group, ratings rescaled to 7/5/3/7/3/7/7, and whys[2], whys[4], whys[5], whys[6] rewritten to agree.

audit.whatIsWrong: Level 6 was written as Warwick's clean-kill spike; the item stages carried no mechanism.
audit.why: Flawless Duet is 16/14.5/13/11.5/10s from 850 range and its stun cancels the Infinite Duress channel, so 6 belongs to her. The item stages come back to Warwick because Jaws of the Beast scales off the target's MAXIMUM health — the bruiser items she buys feed the bite — and Eternal Hunger triples below 25% of Warwick's own health.
audit.corrected: Written into phases[2].why, phases[4].why, spikes[1], spikes[2], spikes[3], mid and late.

audit.whatIsWrong: spikes[1] claims Infinite Duress 'ignores her Flawless Duet (E) stun setup if you R first'.
audit.why: Infinite Duress is flagged channel: interruptible, and Flawless Duet is hard CC — her stun cancels the ult. The ult is a finisher after she has spent E, never an opener. Separately, Defiant Dance reduces PHYSICAL damage during the charge, and Eternal Hunger is bonus magic damage — so her W does nothing about your passive, which is worth stating because it changes when you commit into a charged W.
audit.corrected: Reversed in spikes[1], mid, phases[4].why, breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0].d, breakdown.trading and breakdown.late; the magic-vs-physical point added to mid.

audit.whatIsWrong: Irelia is called 'he'/'his' in tradeGood, dosFull[1].d, breakdown.trading, report[3], breakdown.mid, breakdown.feeding, report[12], breakdown.late, dontsFull[0].d and report[8].
audit.corrected: Corrected in the edits that carry the mechanical fixes.

audit.whatIsWrong: The kit file puts a 'grounding' flag on Flawless Duet.
audit.why: Riot's text says only damaged, stunned and Marked — no grounding. A stun already denies casts, so the flag is probably a parse artefact, and grounding would be a materially different claim (it would deny Jaws of the Beast even outside the stun).
audit.corrected: Not asserted anywhere. Recorded in unverified.

edits.before: Infinite Duress locks Irelia out of her Q-reset dance and ignores her Flawless Duet (E) stun setup if you R first; all-in the moment her Q is down, since your suppression plus Primal Howl fear kills her before she stacks passive.
edits.after: Infinite Duress is a channel and Flawless Duet's stun cancels it outright, so never open a fight with the ult — bait the E first, hold Primal Howl for the Bladesurge chain, then leap once that 16-second stun is spent.

edits.before: This is Irelia's spike; her first bruiser item plus full passive stacks make her Q shred and her E stun combo lethal, so stop face-checking her and only trade when Bladesurge is clearly on cooldown.
edits.after: You hold this stage: Jaws of the Beast scales off her maximum health, so every bruiser item she buys feeds your bite. Trade when Bladesurge (8s at rank 3) is down and let Eternal Hunger pay it back.

edits.before: Fed Irelia with items resets Bladesurge across minions and champions to kite your all-in, her Ionian Fervor passive shreds you, and her E can peel your R; in extended fights she out-DPSes you, so pick her only when isolated and Q-less.
edits.after: She still chains Bladesurge resets off low minions, so never fight her beside a wave. Away from one you hold: Eternal Hunger triples below 25% health and Jaws scales off her maximum health, so the longer an isolated duel runs the worse it gets for her.

edits.before: Through 4-6 you dominate; Blood Hunt closes the gap she'd normally dash away from, Primal Howl fears her mid-combo, and Infinite Duress at 6 locks her out of the reset dance for a clean kill before her item spike.
edits.after: Through 4-5 you hold, but 6 is hers: Flawless Duet's stun cancels Infinite Duress, so the ult is a finisher rather than an opener. Defiant Dance only cuts physical damage — Eternal Hunger is magic and goes straight through it.

edits.before: Once Irelia hits her first item and full passive she flips ahead: chained Bladesurge resets kite your engage, her E stun peels your R, and her stacked shred out-DPSes you, so trade early lane leads for objectives and only all-in an isolated, Q-less Irelia.
edits.after: Her E stun still peels Infinite Duress, so late fights hinge on making her spend it first. Past that you hold the duel: Jaws of the Beast scales off her maximum health and Eternal Hunger triples below 25%, so isolate her away from the wave and never fight beside low minions.

edits.before: Your passive sustain wins extended level-1 auto wars. Identify how Irelia contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Eternal Hunger keys off your own health, healing below 50% and tripling below 25%, so a long level-1 auto war is exactly what you want.
